html:
The Battle of Talas was fought in 751 near the Talas river, on today's border of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. An army of the Abbasid Caliphate defeated a Chinese army of the Tang dynasty. It is the only major battle ever fought between Arab and Chinese armies.

Both empires were pushing into Central Asia. The Tang general Gao Xianzhi had won a string of campaigns in the region and had executed the ruler of Tashkent. The ruler's son called on the Arabs for help, and the Abbasid governor of Khorasan sent an army. During the fighting the Karluks, Turkic nomads serving with the Tang, switched sides, and the Chinese army broke.

The battle is often said to have ended Chinese power in Central Asia, but the real blow came four years later. The An Lushan Rebellion of 755 forced the Tang to pull their armies home, and they never returned. The region then turned steadily toward Islam.

A later story says Chinese prisoners from Talas taught the Arabs to make paper, starting papermaking at Samarkand.
